answer: No. A recorded supervision event or completed reconciliation can be relevant evidence, but neither alone establishes adequate supervision or proper ownership records. Fulfillment requires an applicable legal standard and evidence that the conduct and resulting records satisfy it for the relevant actor, activity and period. The retained provisions supply qualitative requirements and relevant factors, not a rule equating completion of an event with compliance.

claims.inference: Text: responsibility remains with the Product Provider despite outsourcing. Deduction: allocating responsibility or recording an oversight event does not itself establish fulfillment of the substantive requirement.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained circular to the product, entity, activity and assessment period, including relevant conditions or modifications.
An applicable standard for operational soundness and ownership record keeping, and facts showing that standard was met throughout the relevant period.
claims.proposition: Retained responsibility and satisfactory performance are distinct questions.

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

claims.inference: Text: UT 6.11C specifies reasonable care, skill and diligence and ongoing supervision and periodic review in outsourced valuation. Deduction: an event log establishes, at most, evidence of a particular activity; its adequacy depends on substance, continuity and context. Applying this valuation-specific standard to other tokenisation supervision would require a separate legal justification.
missing_premises: That the UT Code applies, the entity is the management company, and the third party performs the relevant valuation activity.
Any applicable authorisation conditions, modifications or relaxations.
Evidence of what was reviewed, by whom, with what competence and resources, at what intervals, and how findings were investigated and addressed.
A justified assessment that the scope, frequency and quality of monitoring met the applicable standard.
claims.proposition: A recorded supervision event does not alone establish adequate ongoing supervision.
claims.status: source-supported deduction; factual adequacy not established

support.quote: Where a third party is engaged in the valuation of a scheme, the management company shall exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in the selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring of such third party in ensuring such entity possesses the appropriate level of knowledge, experience and resources that commensurate with the appropriate valuation policies and procedures for each scheme.
The valuation activities of such third party should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.
This UT Code does not have the force of law.

claims.inference: Text: paragraph 11 requires proper ownership-interest records and operational compatibility; the incorporated considerations include legal validity, regular reconciliations and encumbrances. Deduction: completion of one reconciliation does not establish its accuracy, coverage, exception resolution, or the legal validity of the rights reconciled. Two matching records could share an error.
missing_premises: The governing law, constitutive terms and settlement rules identifying the ownership interests that the records should reflect.
The authoritative records, holders, assets, transactions and period covered by reconciliation.
Evidence of completeness, accuracy, reconciliation frequency, discrepancies and their resolution, and compatibility with relevant service providers.
An applicable interpretation of 'proper records' and evidence that these records meet it; the proposed evidential checks are not an exhaustive source-prescribed test.
claims.proposition: A completed reconciliation is relevant evidence, but does not alone establish proper ownership records.

support.quote: Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.
For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

whether the ownership interest of the underlying assets of the Tokenised Securities are legally valid under the applicable governing laws, whether there are regular reconciliations between the records for the extrinsic rights and the records for the distributed ledger tokens, or whether any encumbrance affects the extrinsic rights.

claims.inference: Text: UT 6.8 assigns register maintenance to specified actors; paragraph 14 separately addresses confirmation and demonstration. Deduction: proving a duty applies, keeping an event log, or obtaining acceptance from a formal solver does not prove performance or regulatory satisfaction.
missing_premises: The actual register-keeper capacity where UT 6.8 is invoked; Product Provider status alone does not establish that capacity.
The relevant SFC request and assessment, if relying on request-triggered demonstration.
A justified source-to-rule interpretation and reliable facts establishing each substantive fulfillment criterion.
claims.proposition: Role-specific duties and demonstration requirements cannot be replaced by a generic event-completion test.

support.quote: The scheme, or in the case of a unit trust, the trustee or the person so appointed by the trustee must maintain a register of holders.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

rival_readings: An allocation-focused reading of paragraph 10 emphasises continued ultimate responsibility; a conduct-focused reading emphasises effective management and oversight; an outcome-focused reading emphasises operational soundness and ownership records. The retained text does not establish that allocation, conduct or outcomes alone are a complete discharge test.

A supervision event or reconciliation may form part of sufficient evidence when its substance and context are established. Treating its mere recorded completion as sufficient has no support in the quoted provisions.
unresolved: No actual supervision records, reconciliation results, ownership terms or assessment-period facts are supplied.
The applicable qualitative standard has not been translated into a justified, fact-sensitive sufficiency test.
The relevance of UT valuation requirements to supervision outside valuation requires an express legal bridge.
Neither duty applicability nor formal acceptance of a proposed rule establishes fulfillment or legal truth.
